reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 FUNCTION MEAN must return the arithmetic mean of its argument series, where the series includes each table element an ALL subscript implies (an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table up to its current count, §1989:A.2.2) and any mix of literals, items, expressions and nested functions.

edition-consulted.switches: the IntroducedIn / RemovedIn window; MEAN's row carries 85

takes the edition year, but only INTEGER's argument rounding under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD depends on it; MEAN keeps all digits and 1985 has no ARITHMETIC clause, so the edition arm is not on this path

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior|ConstructRegistry|.Year over FunctionValueLane.cs, IntrinsicCarrierRules.cs, IntrinsicRenderer.cs, IntrinsicCatalog.cs; the MeanExact / MeanDec choice in IntrinsicRenderer is keyed on num.StandardDecimal (the arithmetic mode), not the edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: mean.cob printed the same 16 lines at --std 85 and --std 2023.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf40_02 covers a mean value. Not exercised by it at 85: an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table with ALL at two different counts, two ALL subscripts, negatives, scaled items, 18-digit operands, nested function arguments, a repeating quotient, and MEAN in a relation; the probes cover them.

reader.notes: MEAN is evaluated as the exact sum divided by the count (MeanExact in native arithmetic, MeanDec under a standard mode), so 18-digit operands do not overflow and a repeating quotient is truncated only by the receiver. The ODO table contributes its current count of elements.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: rmean.cob (rmean-002) exact on all-fixed-point lists: MEAN(99999999999999999 .000000000000000001)=49999999999999999.5, MEAN(.000000000000000003 .000000000000000001)=.000000000000000002, 9PP item 150, VP9 item .025, COMP-3 -0.5, TE(ALL K) 3.85, TE OF TR(ALL ALL) with 0 -> 2.0428 (14.3/7), ROUNDED 5/3 1.6667, ZERO arg 1.5. BUT X8 MEAN(TE(K ALL) TE(1 1) FUNCTION SQRT(4)) printed 2.1599, not 2.16; rmix.cob isolates it: Y1 MEAN(-4.4 5.5 6.6 1.1 2)=2.1600, Y2 MEAN(-4.4 5.5 6.6 1.1 FUNCTION SQRT(4))=2.1599, while rsqrt.cob shows SQRT(4) is exactly 2.00000000000000 and 8.8 + SQRT(4) = 10.8000; same at --std 2023. Cause read in code: CobolIntrinsics.ExactValue.cs#MeanExact calls TryBinary64Body, which evaluates the WHOLE mean in binary64 (MeanReal) once any argument is binary64 (an approximate function such as SQRT), so the exact decimals -4.4..1.1 are converted to doubles and the sum is 10.799999999999999; the reader's note 'the sum is exact before the one division' misses this arm. This is documented as an implementor determination (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-92b.md). Cites: OK §1989:A.2.24.4 RV2 'the sum of the argument-1 series divided by the number of occurrences referenced by argument-1'; OK §1985:IV.4.3.4 'Each implementor will indicate the techniques used in evaluating integer and numeric functions'; §1989:A.2.40.4 RV1 (SQRT is an approximation; cite.py corrected my A.2.41.4 to A.2.40.4). READING: the verdict holds only if §1985:IV.4.3.4's technique latitude (and SQRT being an approximation) licenses evaluating MEAN over EXACT decimal arguments in binary64 when one argument is approximate; against it, RV2 defines the value as sum/count of the argument values, and the compiler's own native expression 8.8 + SQRT(4) stays exact. If the latitude does not stretch that far, the verdict is wrong-answer (truncation to 2.1599), cause (b) same at every edition.

adjudication.reason: The doubt is rejected: §1985:IV.4.3.4 leaves the techniques used in evaluating integer and numeric functions to the implementor, and the register entry DOC-A.1-92b indicates this one (binary64 once any argument is floating-point or an approximation); the entry gains its 1985 sentence.
